result.text:
Team, we need to address the Redis cluster cache stampede that occurred during this morning’s flash sale.

First, please check @config/redis.conf to confirm that `maxmemory-policy` is configured to `volatile-lru` and verify that our client connection pool limits are set to 20,000 connections. Next, inspect @cluster/sentinel.py and @services/cache_manager.ts.

The primary incident trigger was a sudden cache invalidation cascade when 5,000 concurrent checkout workers attempted to recalculate inventory balances simultaneously after key expiration. To prevent recurrent stampedes, we must implement probabilistic early expiration using the XFetch algorithm with a beta value of 1.2 and set background refresh timeouts to 5 seconds.

In addition, update @cluster/sentinel.py to ensure that automatic Sentinel failover triggers after three consecutive unresponsive ping probes spaced 2 seconds apart, rather than the current 30-second timeout. Do not disable master-replica replication sync under any circumstances during failover testing.

The database team lead requires us to verify fallback read throughput against read replicas and establish automated Grafana alerts when the Redis memory fragmentation ratio exceeds 1.5. Also, confirm that all worker threads log Redis connection timeouts to Datadog with structured error tags, including client IP address, tenant ID, and operation latency, before concluding the remediation cycle.

Furthermore, our edge caching layer must enforce a minimum time to live of 120 seconds on inventory metadata to avoid upstream Redis queries during momentary network partitions between edge gateways and core database pods. The reliability engineering team will run automated load tests simulating 15,000 transactions per second against the staging cluster to ensure latency remains under 25 milliseconds across 99% of requests.

Regarding Sentinel cluster quorum, we must verify that all three Sentinel pods run in independent availability zones and configure `down-after-milliseconds` to 5,000 milliseconds across each node. The client connection pools in the auth service and order worker must initialize backoff retries using full jitter, with a base interval of 100 milliseconds capped at 2,000 milliseconds.

Incident coordinators should also review @docs/runbooks/redis_failover.md to ensure that emergency manual failover procedures accurately reflect the latest cluster endpoint topology. We must also confirm that Redis persistent append-only files are synced every second on replica disks and verify that background rewrite tasks do not trigger memory allocation spikes during active peak traffic windows.

Finally, schedule an operational readiness review for Thursday afternoon with the infrastructure engineering manager to audit all configuration diffs and approve deployment to production.
